title: On OpenShift the 1.10 seccomp profile can be rejected by SecurityContextConstraints

detection.reason: SecurityContextConstraints is an OpenShift admission object the agent does not collect, and whether THIS cluster's SCC admits a RuntimeDefault seccomp profile depends on the OpenShift version and its configuration

quote: In cert-manager 1.10 the secure computing (seccomp) profile for all the Pods is set to `RuntimeDefault`. On some versions and configurations of OpenShift this can cause the Pod to be rejected by the Security Context Constraints admission webhook.
remediation: On OpenShift, confirm the cert-manager ServiceAccounts are admitted by an SCC that allows the RuntimeDefault seccomp profile before upgrading.
verifyCommand: kubectl get securitycontextconstraints -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | "\(.metadata.name) seccompProfiles=\(.seccompProfiles // [] | join(","))"'  # no output = not OpenShift; otherwise an SCC must allow runtime/default

title: The controller and webhook containers are renamed — automation keyed on `cert-manager` breaks

detection.reason: the container name is projected; whether any script, log query or sidecar config keys on it is not a cluster fact

quote: The names are changed to better reflect what they do; for example, the container in the controller pod had its name changed from `cert-manager` to `cert-manager-controller`, and the webhook pod had its container name changed from `cert-manager` to `cert-manager-webhook`.
remediation: Update anything that addresses the container by name (kubectl logs -c, log pipelines, monitoring selectors) to `cert-manager-controller` and `cert-manager-webhook`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("cert-manager")) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name): \([.spec.template.spec.containers[].name] | join(","))"'  # a container still named plain cert-manager is renamed by 1.10
